# The generated host

Next.js needs an `app/` directory of route files. In a NextSpark project that directory, **`src/app`, is generated and git-ignored**: you never write, edit or commit it.

## What is in it

Each file is a thin facade of one module, with fixed imports and no run-time lookup:

```ts
// Generated by NextSpark from @nextsparkjs/core/routes/(auth)/login/page. Do not edit: regenerated on every build.
export { default } from "@nextsparkjs/core/routes/(auth)/login/page"
export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"
```

The module comes from one of three layers, the higher one replacing the lower at the same route file:

| Layer | Where | Route |
| --- | --- | --- |
| core | `@nextsparkjs/core/routes/*`, listed in core's route manifest | the framework's pages, layouts and APIs |
| plugin | `plugins/<name>/templates/**` and `plugins/<name>/api/**` | `templates/**` at the same path; `api/**` at `/api/plugins/<name>/**` |
| project | `templates/**` and `api/**` at the project root | `templates/**` at the same path; `api/**` at `/api/**` |

Next.js reads segment config (`dynamic`, `revalidate`, ...) statically from the route file itself, which is why the facade repeats it as a literal. A source module whose segment config is not a literal, or whose exports Next does not accept for that kind of file, stops generation with the file and export named.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `nextspark dev` | Generates the host and the registries, then runs Next.js and regenerates when the project's source changes (`templates/`, `api/`, `entities/`, `config/`, `blocks/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `messages/`, `styles/`, `nextspark.config.ts`, ...) |
| `nextspark build` | `prepare --production`, then `next build` |
| `nextspark prepare` | Generates `src/app` and `.nextspark/registries` once |
| `nextspark prepare --check` | Exits non-zero unless `src/app` and the registries are exactly what a generation would write |
| `nextspark prepare --watch` | The watcher `dev` runs |

`package.json` scripts call these (`"dev": "nextspark dev"`, `"build": "nextspark build"`). A script that runs `next build` directly skips the generation: run `nextspark prepare` first.

`src/app` is only written when it is generated: a directory that holds anything else is refused, and files that were edited by hand are named instead of overwritten. `.nextspark/generation.json` records what was generated and which inputs.

## Changing a route

- **Replace a page or layout:** put a file at the same path in `templates/` (`templates/dashboard/page.tsx` replaces core's dashboard page). Core protects a few routes that cannot be replaced; the generator says which.
- **Add a page:** the same, at a path core has no route for.
- **Add or replace a Route Handler:** `api/<path>/route.ts` is served at `/api/<path>`. Core owns `/api/v1/**` and each plugin owns `/api/plugins/<name>/**`: a project route there is refused, and a deliberate override of a core handler goes through `templates/api/v1/.../route.ts`. The generic handler of one of your entities can be replaced the same way, at `templates/api/v1/<entity>/route.ts`, `[id]/route.ts`, `[id]/child/[childType]/route.ts` or `[id]/child/[childType]/[childId]/route.ts` (auth, permissions and hooks are then yours: [overriding an entity's API](../05-api/04-custom-endpoints.md#overriding-an-entitys-api)).
- **API Explorer docs:** `docs.md` and `presets.ts` next to a handler are what the explorer shows; core's live next to its route modules in the package.
- **Billing webhook hooks:** `billing.webhookExtensions` in `nextspark.config.ts` names the module that adds one-time payment handling to core's Stripe or Polar webhook.

Rendering mode: Cache Components with PPR is the default for new projects (their `next.config.mjs` sets `cacheComponents: true` and the host emits the Cache Components / PPR variants of core's layouts and public pages, [PPR guide](../13-performance/ppr-migration.md)). Legacy ISR stays supported: remove the setting or set it to `false`. Next.js is pinned to `~16.3.6`.

## Upgrading

A project created before `0.1.0-beta.192` has a committed `src/app`: [upgrade it with `nextspark migrate`](../17-updates/06-upgrade-0x-projects.md). `nextspark sync:app` no longer exists ([timeline](../17-updates/05-sync-app-removal.md)).
